About our Data

This project combines 2019 data from the Smart Location Database and Pedestrian Crash Data to provide a snapshot of how walkability infleunces multiple facets of life. Links to each database can be found below.

Smart Location Database (with Walkability Index)

https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/smart-location-database8

Pedestrian Crash Data

https://www.nhtsa.gov/file-downloads?p=nhtsa/downloads/FARS/

Employment and Walkability

Completed by Cheyna Warner

Column

Unemployment Rates

Column

About

This plot shows the relationship between walkability and employment rates.

Hypothesis: I hypothesize that unemployment rates will be greater in less walkable areas.

Conclusions: Walkability and unemployment rates have a significant, negative relationship.

Unemployment Rates Plot v1

Unemployment Rates Plot v2

Number of Cars

Completed by Cheyna Warner

Column

Households with > 1 cars

Column

About

This graph shows the relationship between walkability and number of households that own at least 1 car.

Hypothesis: I hypothesize that people who live in walkable areas will have fewer cars.

Conclusions: Walkability and number of cars have a significant, positive relationship.
